questions.question:
There are four underlined words in the sentence given below. One of them is misspelt. Choose the option with the misspelt word.
The opposition demanded accountability, citing falsified data, embezzelment of funds, and corruption in high offices.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**embezzelment**__.

**__Key Points__**

__

• The word **embezzelment** is misspelt in the provided sentence. The correct spelling is **embezzlement**.

• The term is a **derivative noun** formed by adding the suffix **-ment** to the root verb **embezzle**, which means to secretly take money that is in your care but belongs to an organization or another person.

• According to **English orthography**, when a suffix is added to a word ending in **-le**, the existing letters remain in their original order. In this case, **-le-** should precede the **-ment**, not **-el-**.

• From a **legal standpoint**, **embezzlement** is a **white-collar crime** characterized by the fraudulent misappropriation of assets by a person in a position of trust or **fiduciary responsibility**.

• Statistically, cases of **embezzlement** often involve **financial sectors** where internal controls are bypassed to hide the theft of **liquid assets** or company funds over long periods.

 **Additional Information__**

• **accountability**

• Refers to the **institutionalized expectation** that public and private agents will provide information about their actions and justify them.

• It serves as a core component of **democratic governance** and **corporate ethics**, ensuring **transparency** and reducing **malpractice**.

• **falsified**

• This is the **past participle** of the verb **falsify**, which involves altering information to make it incorrect or deceptive.

• In **forensic auditing**, **falsified data** refers to manipulated financial records used to cover up **illicit transactions** or inflate company value.

• **corruption**

• Defined as the **abuse of entrusted power** for private gain, often measured globally by the **Corruption Perceptions Index (CPI)**.

• It encompasses various activities including **bribery**, **extortion**, **nepotism**, and **money laundering**.

</ul

questions.question:
Which of the following options is the most suitable conversion of the following sentence into Passive Voice?
They will have completed the construction of the new bridge by the end of this year.

options.text: The construction of the new bridge is completed by them by the end of this year.
The construction of the new bridge will be completed by them by the end of this year.
The construction of the new bridge will have completed by them by the end of this year.
The construction of the new bridge will have been completed by them by the end of this year.

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**The construction of the new bridge will have been completed by them by the end of this year.**__.

**__Key Points__**

__
 
• To convert a sentence from **Active Voice** to **Passive Voice**, we must first identify the **tense** of the original sentence. The sentence 'They will have completed the construction of the new bridge by the end of this year' is in the **Future Perfect Tense**.
 
• In the **Active Voice**, the **Future Perfect Tense** follows the structure: **Subject + will + have + Past Participle (V3) + Object**. In this sentence, **They** is the subject and **the construction of the new bridge** is the object.
 
• When converting to **Passive Voice**, the **Object** of the active sentence becomes the **New Subject**. Thus, **the construction of the new bridge** starts the passive sentence.
 
• The **verb transformation** for **Future Perfect Passive** requires the addition of the auxiliary verb **been**. The formula is: **New Subject + will + have + been + V3 + by + Agent**.
 
• Therefore, **will have completed** is transformed into **will have been completed**. The original subject **They** is converted into the agent **them** following the preposition **by**.
 
• The **time phrase** 'by the end of this year' remains at the end of the sentence to provide the **context of completion** in the future.

 **Additional Information__**

 
• **Future Perfect Tense** characteristics:
 
 
• It expresses an action that will be **certainly completed** by a specific point in the future.
 
• In passive transformations, the inclusion of **been** is mandatory to distinguish it from the **Future Continuous** or **Simple Future**.
 
 
 
• Evaluation of incorrect structures:
 
 
• **Simple Future Passive**: Uses 'will be completed', which fails to capture the **perfective aspect** (the completion) of the original statement.
 
• **Present Passive**: Uses 'is completed', which changes the **temporal frame** from the future to the present.
 
• **Grammatical Omission**: Sentences that omit **been** while using **will have** remain in an **incomplete active form** and do not function as passive voice.
 
 
</ul

questions.question:
Which of the following options is the most suitable conversion of the following sentence into Passive Voice?
Despite aiming carefully, the hunter missed the deer.

options.text: The deer was aimed carefully by the hunter but missed.
The deer was missed by the hunter despite aiming carefully.
The deer is missed by the hunter despite aiming carefully.
The deer will be missed by the hunter despite aiming carefully.

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**The deer was missed by the hunter despite aiming carefully.**__.

**__Key Points__**

__

• The sentence provided is in the **Active Voice**, following the structure: **Subject** (the hunter) + **Verb** (missed) + **Object** (the deer).

• The verb **missed** is in the **Simple Past Tense**. According to the rules of English grammar, the **Passive Voice** for the **Simple Past Tense** is formed using **was/were + Past Participle (V3)**.

• To transform the sentence, the **Object** of the active voice (**the deer**) is moved to the **Subject** position. Since **the deer** is a **singular noun**, the auxiliary verb **was** is required.

• The **Past Participle** form of the verb **miss** is **missed**, which remains consistent in both forms but serves as the **V3** component here.

• The original **Subject** (**the hunter**) becomes the **Agent** in the passive sentence and is preceded by the preposition **by**.

• The **adverbial phrase** **despite aiming carefully** is a modifier that describes the circumstances of the action; it is retained to ensure the **semantic integrity** and **contextual meaning** of the original sentence are preserved.

 **Additional Information__**

• **Grammatical Tense Consistency**:

• In voice conversion, the **tense** of the original sentence must not change. The use of **is missed** would incorrectly shift the sentence into the **Simple Present Tense**.

• The use of **will be missed** would incorrectly shift the sentence into the **Simple Future Tense**, which describes an event that has not yet occurred.

• **Logical Subject-Object Relationship**:

• The construction **was aimed carefully by the hunter** changes the **primary action** of the sentence from missing to aiming, which deviates from the **original intent** of the active sentence where the main action is the failure to hit the target (missing).

</ul

questions.question:
Select the correct alternative to fill in the blank with the correct preposition in the following sentence.

The soldier died while fighting against the terrorists just a few days shy _____ his marriage anniversary.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is '**of**'. **__Key Points__** __ 
• The word **shy**, when followed by the **preposition 'of'**, forms an idiomatic expression. 
• The phrase **shy of** means **short of**, **less than**, or **just before** reaching a specific amount, level, or point in time. 
• In the given sentence, it indicates that the **soldier** died just a few days **before** he could celebrate his **marriage anniversary**. 
• Other options like **for**, **by**, or **to** do not form a standard idiom with **shy** to convey the intended meaning of being **nearly at a milestone**. Therefore, the correct answer is **Option 2**. **Complete Sentence:** *'The soldier died while fighting against the terrorists just a few days **shy of**__ his marriage anniversary.'* **__Additional Information__** 
• **Option 1: 'for'** is typically used to indicate a **duration** or a **purpose** (e.g., waiting for hours). 
• **Option 3: 'by'** is often used to show **proximity**, **agency**, or a **deadline** (e.g., finished by noon). 
• **Option 4: 'to'** is generally used to indicate **direction**, **destination**, or **comparison**. </ul

• While the original word **cooperatively** suggests working together or being helpful to one another, it is less idiomatic than **collectively** when describing a **mass resignation** or a joint formal action.
 
• The structure **in protest against** is the standard prepositional phrase used to denote that an action is taken to demonstrate **strong disapproval** or **opposition** toward a specific entity, such as **unethical management practices**.
 
• Using **collectively** improves the sentence by emphasizing that the resignation was not just a series of individual acts but a **coordinated effort** by the entire **committee**.

 **Additional Information__**

 
• **Communally**:
 
 
• This refers to things **shared** by all members of a community or group for **common use**.
 
• It typically applies to **living arrangements**, **dining**, or **resource management** within a community.
 
 
 
• **Cohesively**:
 
 
• This adverb describes the quality of **sticking together** or functioning as a **well-integrated** whole.
 
• It usually refers to how a group **collaborates** or **interacts** (e.g., a cohesively functioning team) rather than the specific act of **leaving an organization**.
 
 
</ul

questions.question:
A part of the following sentence is underlined. Choose the option that can replace the underlined part to improve the sentence. If you feel Options A, B, or C do not improve the sentence, then choose Option D: "No improvement required."
The novel's plot was so intricate and captivating, it was impossible for the reader to predict the ending.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**that it was impossible**__.

**__Key Points__**

__

• The sentence requires the use of a **correlative conjunction** to link the degree of an attribute to its result. The standard structure used in English for this purpose is **so + adjective/adverb + that**.

• In this context, **so** modifies the adjectives **intricate** and **captivating**, while the word **that** introduces the **subordinate clause** explaining the consequence (the impossibility of predicting the ending).

• While the word **that** is occasionally omitted in informal spoken English, formal writing and competitive examinations require its inclusion to avoid a **comma splice** and to clearly establish the **cause-and-effect** relationship.

• By replacing the comma and the following phrase with **that it was impossible**, the sentence achieves grammatical completeness and logical flow.

 **Additional Information__**

• **Correlative Structures**:

• **So... that**: Used with adjectives or adverbs to show degree and result (e.g., **so fast that**).

• **Such... that**: Used with **noun phrases** to show degree and result (e.g., **such an intricate plot that**).

• **Too... to**: Used to indicate a negative consequence due to excess (e.g., **too intricate to predict**).

• **Analysis of Incorrect Options**:

• **so it was impossible**: This creates a **redundancy** because the word **so** is already present earlier in the sentence. Using it twice as a conjunction and an intensifier in this manner is non-standard.

• **as to not be possible**: This phrase follows the **so + adjective + as to + verb** construction. However, it is wordy, less direct, and typically used when the subject of both clauses is the same. In the original sentence, the **reader** (implicit or explicit) is the one facing the impossibility, making the **that clause** more appropriate.

</ul

questions.question:
Identify the error in the given following question :
I went to my school with a view to meet the principal.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is **Option 3**.

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The error in the sentence is the use of the base form of the verb **meet** after the phrase **with a view to**.
 
• The expression **with a view to** is a phrasal preposition that must be followed by a **gerund** (the -ing form of a verb).
 
• A **gerund** acts as a noun, which is required after the preposition **to** in this specific idiomatic context.
 
• Therefore, the verb **meet** should be changed to **meeting** to make the sentence grammatically accurate.
 
• Thus, the error is located in **part 3** of the sentence.

Therefore, the correct answer is **3**.

 

**Correct Sentence:** *'I went to my school **with a view to meeting** the principal.'*

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Option 1: 'i went to my school'** – This part contains the subject and the main verb in the past tense, which is grammatically correct.
 
• **Option 2: 'with a view to'** – This is a standard idiomatic phrase meaning 'with the intention of'. It is used correctly as a linker here.
 
• **Option 4: 'the principal'** – This is the object of the gerund and is used correctly with the definite article.
 
• Similar phrases that are followed by a **gerund** instead of an infinitive include: **look forward to**, **accustomed to**, **used to** (when preceded by a 'be' verb), and **given to**.
 
• Example: *'He is looking forward to **visiting** the museum.'*
</ul

questions.question:

If you had told me earlier, I will have helped you.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is **Option 3**.

 

**__Key Points__**

__
 
• The sentence provided is an example of a **Third Conditional** sentence, which is used to talk about a situation that did not happen in the past and its imaginary result.
 
• The grammatical structure for the **Third Conditional** is: **If + Past Perfect (had + V3)**, **would have + Past Participle (V3)**.
 
• In the clause 'If you had told me earlier,' the **past perfect** tense (**had told**) is used correctly.
 
• However, the main clause '**I will have**' incorrectly uses the future tense auxiliary 'will' instead of the conditional '**would**.'
 
• The correct phrase should be '**I would have**' to maintain grammatical harmony in a third conditional construction.
 
• Therefore, the error is located in **part 3** of the sentence.

Therefore, the correct answer is **I will have**.

 

**Correct Sentence:** *'If you had told me earlier, **I would have** helped you.'*

 

**Additional Information__**

 
• **if you had told** – This part of the sentence correctly establishes the hypothetical past condition using the **past perfect** tense.
 
• **me earlier,** – This is an adverbial phrase modifying the verb and is grammatically correct.
 
• **helped you** – This is the correct **past participle (V3)** form of the verb 'help,' which is required following 'have' in this structure.
</ul

In the following question, the first and the last parts of the sentence/passage are numbered 1 and 6. The rest of the sentence/passage is split into four parts - P, Q, R, and S. These four parts are not given in their proper order. Read the sentence/passage and find the most logical order of the parts between 1 and 6.

1. A farmer works hard every day to grow food for everyone. 

P. He wakes up early and goes to the field before sunrise. 

Q. He works under the hot sun and heavy rain without rest. 

R. His patience and effort bring a good harvest after many months. 

S. He ploughs the land, sows the seeds, and waters the crops carefully. 

6. The farmer's hard work feeds the nation and deserves great respect.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is **Option 3**.

 

**__Key Points__**

 
• The passage follows a chronological and logical sequence describing the life and work of a **farmer**, starting from his daily routine to the final result of his labor. 
• **Sentence 1** introduces the topic: 'A farmer works hard every day to grow food for everyone.' 
• **Sentence P follows** as it describes the very beginning of his day, which is the logical next step after the introduction: 
• 'He **wakes up early** and goes to the **field** before sunrise.' 
• **Sentence S is the third sentence** because it details the specific agricultural tasks he performs once he is at the field: 
• 'He **ploughs the land**, **sows the seeds**, and **waters the crops** carefully.' 
• **Sentence Q is the fourth sentence** as it describes the physical conditions and perseverance required while performing those tasks: 
• 'He works under the **hot sun** and **heavy rain** without rest.' 
• **Sentence R is the fifth sentence** because it highlights the outcome of his long-term effort and patience: 
• 'His patience and effort bring a **good harvest** after many months.' 
• Finally, **Sentence 6** concludes the passage by stating the social importance of his work: 'The farmer's hard work **feeds the nation** and deserves **great respect**.' 
• The correct logical sequence is **PSQR**. 

 

**Coherent paragraph after rearrangement**:

'A farmer works hard every day to grow food for everyone. He wakes up early and goes to the field before sunrise. He ploughs the land, sows the seeds, and waters the crops carefully. He works under the hot sun and heavy rain without rest. His patience and effort bring a good harvest after many months. The farmer's hard work feeds the nation and deserves great respect.'</div

These four parts are not given in their proper order. Read the sentence/passage and find the most logical order of the parts between 1 and 6.

1. The carpenter was working on the new table. 

P. He measured the wood carefully.

Q. Then he began to smooth the edges. 

R. Next, he joined the legs with glue. 

S. He cut the parts as per the plan. 

6. Finally, he polished the surface.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is **Option 2**.

 

**__Key Points__**

 
• The passage describes a **logical, step-by-step process** of a **carpenter** building a **new table**, starting from preparation and ending with the final finish. 
• **Sentence P is the first sentence** after the introduction because **measuring** is the foundational first step in any woodworking project: 
• 'He **measured the wood** carefully.' 
• **Sentence S follows P** as the next logical action after measurement is to **cut** the material according to those dimensions: 
• 'He **cut the parts** as per the plan.' 
• **Sentence Q is the third sentence**, indicated by the transition word **'Then'**. After cutting, the **edges** of the pieces are typically **smoothed** before they are assembled: 
• 'Then he began to **smooth the edges**.' 
• **Sentence R is the fourth sentence**, introduced by **'Next'**. This sentence describes the **assembly phase** where the structural components are **joined**: 
• 'Next, he **joined the legs** with glue.' 
• The sequence concludes with sentence 6, which uses the word **'Finally'** to describe the **polishing** of the finished surface. 
• The correct sequence is **PSQR**.
